Target  synthetic-two  · current Git branch

  ○ synthetic-main   trunk
  ├─● synthetic-one  #41  base✓  merge
  └─● synthetic-two  #42  head✗ publish first  base✗ → synthetic-main  merge with --admin  ← target

Commands this would run, in order
   1  g2g_landed_41=$(git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/synthetic-one)  · remember the head about to merge, which the merge and the deletion after it are pinned to
   2  gh pr merge 41 --squash --match-head-commit "${g2g_landed_41:?}"  · land synthetic-one
   3  g2g pull --apply  · advance the trunk and replay what is left onto it
   4  g2g prune --branch synthetic-one --scope branch --apply  · forget it, once what sat on it has been reparented
   5  git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/synthetic-one:"${g2g_landed_41:?}" origin --delete refs/heads/synthetic-one  · remove the published branch while it is still what landed, if the merge has not already
   6  git branch -D synthetic-one  · remove it here
   7  g2g push --branch synthetic-two --scope path --apply  · publish it as it is here
   8  gh pr edit 42 --base synthetic-main  · merge into synthetic-main rather than synthetic-one
   9  g2g_landed_42=$(git rev-parse --verify refs/heads/synthetic-two)  · remember the head about to merge, which the merge and the deletion after it are pinned to
  10  gh pr merge 42 --squash --match-head-commit "${g2g_landed_42:?}" --admin  · land synthetic-two
  11  g2g pull --apply  · advance the trunk and replay what is left onto it
  12  g2g prune --branch synthetic-two --scope branch --apply  · forget it, once what sat on it has been reparented
  13  git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/synthetic-two:"${g2g_landed_42:?}" origin --delete refs/heads/synthetic-two  · remove the published branch while it is still what landed, if the merge has not already
  14  git branch -D synthetic-two  · remove it here
